FQ_RESULTS_CARRIED.exact_object_basis: The candidate delta is a single file addition of one blob. There is no second file, no incidental edit, no protected-surface write and no scope leak. The object on disk is the object attested.
FQ_RESULTS_CARRIED.semantic_basis: The audited object freezes index dispositions that were not measured against the schema state they claim to describe. See F-FQ-1.
FQ_RESULTS_CARRIED.why_both_verdicts_stand: Exact-object PASS and semantic FAIL are orthogonal axes and do not contradict each other. blocking.not_blocking_for: The integrated docs-only amendment itself, which is already merged and is not retracted by this artifact.
blocking.finding: I-1, I-2 and I-4 were frozen as REQUIRED_NEW without measuring their existing full-tuple UNIQUE constraints. Each of the three relations already carries a UNIQUE constraint over exactly the column list the proposed index would create.

independent_re_derivation_by_LANE_FS.note: LANE FS did not accept F-FQ-1 on assertion. It re-derived the finding from the migration corpus and from the live schema snapshot.
independent_re_derivation_by_LANE_FS.M1: All three UNIQUE constraints are present in the migrations that create their relations (0045, 0048, 0053).
independent_re_derivation_by_LANE_FS.M2: All three UNIQUE constraints are still live at the most recent schema snapshot, db/migrations/meta/0067_snapshot.json, under uniqueConstraints with exactly the column lists above. They were not dropped after creation.
independent_re_derivation_by_LANE_FS.M3: In PostgreSQL a UNIQUE table constraint is implemented by an automatically created unique btree index over exactly those columns in that order. The audited object itself states this rule at evidence anchor B10 and relies on it to discharge I-13 against FIBDB-022.
independent_re_derivation_by_LANE_FS.M4: A btree index supports backward scans, so an index recorded ASC serves DESC ordering over the same column list. The 'ordinal DESC' spelling in the proposed definitions does not create a requirement the existing constraint-backed index fails to satisfy.
independent_re_derivation_by_LANE_FS.M5: The precedent for the correct disposition exists inside the audited object itself. I-11 was dispositioned ALREADY_SATISFIED_AT_AS_OF_HEAD precisely because uq_readiness_assessments_calculation_run was measured and found to exist. I-1, I-2 and I-4 sit in the same evidence class and received the opposite disposition.

scope_precision_confirmed.I-3_correctly_excluded: I-3 is a PARTIAL index on evidence_versions (evidence_id) WHERE review_status='approved'. A full-tuple UNIQUE over (evidence_id, ordinal) does not satisfy a partial predicate index, so I-3 is correctly left as REQUIRED_NEW and is NOT part of this finding.
scope_precision_confirmed.I-6_I-8_I-9_I-12_are_a_different_axis: Those four are already recorded by the audited object's own F-A1 as the INVERSE relation: the proposed two-column index subsumes an existing single-column index. F-FQ-1 is the direction F-A1 never ran, where an existing constraint-backed index subsumes the PROPOSED index.

blocking.why_it_is_blocking: An implementing mission reading this frozen inventory would emit three CREATE INDEX statements that duplicate existing constraint-backed indexes, and would then verify them by exact name under COMPLETION_SEMANTICS C2/C3/C4/C6 and record a satisfied obligation. The defect is not merely a redundant index: it is that a disposition was frozen without the measurement that the same artifact applied elsewhere, so the error would be ratified rather than caught.
blocking.direct_contradiction_recorded: The audited object self-declares OPEN_FINDINGS.blocking_for_fibdb052_implementation = [] and self_check.expected_blocking_count = 0. F-FQ-1 contradicts that self-assessment. The self-assessment is not evidence against the finding; it is the surface the finding falsifies.
blocking.resolution_owner: A successor disposition-correction authority. NOT this artifact.

non_blocking.finding: Evidence anchor B18 states that the longest index identifier existing at AS_OF_HEAD is idx_evidence_sufficiency_determinations_outcome_run at 51 characters. When constraint-backed indexes are included - consistently with B10's own treatment of UNIQUE table constraints as index-producing objects - the actual longest existing identifier is evidence_sufficiency_determinations_outcome_run_ordinal_unique at 62 characters, one below PostgreSQL's 63-byte identifier limit.
non_blocking.root_cause: The same measurement inconsistency as F-FQ-1: the audited object counts UNIQUE constraint-backed indexes when discharging some obligations, but excludes them when measuring the existing-index identifier population.

independent_re_derivation_by_LANE_FS.M1: Length of idx_evidence_sufficiency_determinations_outcome_run = 51 characters. CONFIRMED, matching B18.
independent_re_derivation_by_LANE_FS.M3: Both identifiers are created by the SAME migration file on adjacent lines: db/migrations/0052_fib_evidence_sufficiency_run_binding.sql:26 creates the index, and :27 adds the UNIQUE constraint. The longer identifier was not remote from the measurement; it was one line away.
independent_re_derivation_by_LANE_FS.M4: B18 cites its source as 'db/schema.ts plus INDEX_NAMING_RULE.self_check_lengths'. A sweep of declared indexes in db/schema.ts structurally cannot see an identifier generated by a table constraint, which explains the omission without excusing it.
independent_re_derivation_by_LANE_FS.M5: B10 of the same artifact explicitly holds that a UNIQUE table constraint is implemented by an automatically created unique btree index. The two anchors apply opposite rules to the same class of object.

non_blocking.disposition: NON_BLOCKING. B18's operative safety conclusion survives.
